posts.text:
Agent coding life hack:

I'm 100% convinced that there are hundreds of thousands of developers out there who would love and use my dcg tool if they only knew about it.

dcg: destructive_command_guard

This is a free, open-source, highly-optimized rust program that runs using pre-tool hooks in Claude Code (CC) and checks the tool call that CC was about to make to see if it's potentially destructive...

Get it here and install with the convenient one-liner:
https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/destructive_command_guard

[Full text: 5-point breakdown of dcg goals: speed (SIMD/Rust), no false positives, AST-grep heredoc detection, 50+ preset packs, agent-friendly explanations with safe alternatives.]

dcg is included along with all my other tooling in my http://agent-flywheel.com project.
posts.notes: DCG deep-dive post. 120K views, 1304 bookmarks — highest bookmarks of any Jan post. Pre-tool hook safety guard for Claude Code. AST-grep heredoc detection, SIMD regex, 50+ preset packs. Existing catalogue entry at research/catalogue/agent-harnesses/ likely covers DCG but this post is the canonical promotion thread.

posts.text:
I'm living this every day, and let me tell you, things are accelerating very rapidly indeed.

Using skills to improve skills, skills to improve tool use, and then feeding the actual experience in the form of session logs (surfaced and searched by my cass tool and /cass skill) back into the design skill...

[Full text: vision post on recursive self-improvement loop — skills improve tools, tools improve skills, session logs feed back into design. Mentions asupersync, process_triage (pt), Flywheel Connector Protocol, porting rich/fastapi/fastmcp/sqlmodel from Python + Charm libs from Go + OpenTUI. All repos public.]
posts.notes: Major vision post. Describes recursive flywheel: skills → tools → session logs → improved design → better skills. Introduces asupersync (Tokio replacement), process_triage (pt), Flywheel Connector Protocol. Lists all Python/Go libs being ported to Rust. Teases FrankenLib merge. High substantive signal.

posts.text:
I mentioned recently that I've been... busy. Lots of projects in the oven, in various stages of completeness.

Well, I'm now pleased to introduce one I've worked very hard on, because it's so near-and-dear to my heart:

beads_rust, or br for short. You can get it here:

https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust

It's a fast, minimal Rust port of @Steve_Yegge's amazing Beads project...

[Full text: explains divergence from Steve Yegge's beads roadmap toward GasTown; justification for freezing hybrid SQLite+JSONL-git architecture in Rust port. br vs bd naming distinction. Steve Yegge endorsement.]
posts.notes: beads_rust announcement post. Rust port of Steve Yegge's Beads. Freezes hybrid SQLite+JSONL-git architecture. Steve Yegge endorsed. 64K views, 184 bookmarks. Key catalogue-worthy post — beads_rust is an existing entry in agent-harnesses/pi/ family.
